title: Late Breaking Results: Machine Learning Based Reference Ripple Error Suppression in Successive Approximation Register Analog-to-Digital Converters
problem: Reference voltage ripple in SAR ADCs introduces dynamic errors that manifest as spurs in the output spectrum, limiting ADC resolution. Conventional suppression requires large decoupling capacitors and high-speed reference buffers consuming significant area and power.
motivation: Reducing power consumption and area overhead in ADC designs while maintaining signal fidelity is critical for efficient analog signal processing.
method: A supervised machine learning approach uses a low-speed 10MHz SAR ADC to learn and predict reference ripple errors occurring in a 200MHz SAR ADC. The ML model corrects ripple-induced dynamic errors in real-time, eliminating the need for large passive decoupling components and high-speed buffers. The design is simulated in 28nm CMOS technology.
key_novelty: Using supervised learning from a low-speed reference ADC to predict and correct reference ripple errors in a high-speed SAR ADC, eliminating conventional hardware-intensive suppression.
contributions: ML-based technique for real-time reference ripple error suppression in SAR ADCs
4.9x power consumption reduction while maintaining ADC resolution
Elimination of area-intensive decoupling capacitors and high-speed reference buffers
Dual-ADC learning architecture that leverages low-speed and high-speed converters

metrics.accuracy: maintained ADC resolution with no performance degradation

baselines: conventional SAR ADC with passive ripple suppression
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation limited to simulations without silicon validation or practical implementation results.
primary_theme: ML-based optimization for analog SAR ADC circuits
